metaDescription: Six cordless chainsaws compared on bar length, voltage, brushless motor, chain brake, tool free tensioning, weight and battery, with picks for homeowners.
expertTake: The EGO Power+ CS1613 16 inch is our top pick because of its brushless motor, a stated gas equivalent power class and a tool free chain system on a well supported battery platform. The Greenworks 40V 12 inch is the value pick for limbing and storm cleanup around a typical yard. Skip a mini chainsaw for anything beyond pruning, because they are built for small branches and a one handed grip is a poor way to control a saw.
introParagraphs: A cordless chainsaw swaps the two stroke engine for a brushless motor and a lithium ion battery. It starts instantly, needs no fuel mixing and runs far quieter than gas, which makes it a good fit for homeowners who cut a few trees, limbs and logs a year.

The real choices are bar length, battery voltage and capacity, weight and the safety features that control kickback. We evaluated six models from the candidate pool using spec sheets, listing details and owner feedback patterns, then ranked them by fit for typical yard work. A chainsaw is a dangerous tool, so protective gear and training matter more than any spec.

products.name: EGO Power+ CS1613 16 inch 56V cordless chainsaw with 4.0Ah battery and charger
products.description:
The CS1613 has a 16 inch bar with a 3/8 inch pitch, 0.043 inch gauge chain with 56 drive links, a brushless motor and a 4.0Ah battery included. The maker describes the power as equivalent to a 40 cc gas saw, a comparison that is a marketing class, not a measurement.

The listing says the included battery delivers up to 130 cuts on a 4x4. That is useful for judging how much work one charge does, but cut counts depend on wood species and moisture. Against the Greenworks 80V 16 inch, the EGO has a lower voltage but a larger battery and a widely supported platform. Against the SEESII 40V 16 inch, it is a more established brand with parts support.

Check the bar oil level before each use and clean the chain brake area. Keep the chain sharp, because a dull chain forces you to push, which is when kickback risk rises. Owners often say that a second battery is the best accessory, because a firewood session eats through one pack quicker than the cut count suggests.
products.bestFor: Homeowners with trees and firewood who want a trusted battery platform.
pros: Brushless 56V motor with a stated 40 cc gas class of power
16 inch bar handles most yard trees and firewood
Included 4.0Ah battery gives a good number of cuts per charge
Wide parts and battery support across the EGO range
cons: Upper price tier for a homeowner saw
Battery is heavy, so the saw is not light
Still needs protective gear and training

products.name: Greenworks 80V 16 inch cordless chainsaw kit, 2.5Ah battery, brushless, mechanical chain brake
products.description:
The Greenworks 80V chainsaw includes a 16 inch bar, a brushless motor, a 2.5Ah battery and a mechanical chain brake. The listing says it has twice the torque of the previous design and gives power equivalent to a 50 cc gas engine, which is again a marketing class.

The 80V platform is the highest voltage here and gives a strong cut, but a 2.5Ah battery limits runtime, so expect fewer cuts per charge than the EGO's 4.0Ah pack. The mechanical chain brake adds a layer of safety, stopping the chain when the front guard is pushed forward. Against the EGO CS1613, the Greenworks has more headline voltage and a smaller battery. Against the Greenworks 40V 12 inch, it cuts larger logs at a higher tier.

Check the chain brake works each time before cutting and lubricate the bar. Keep the battery cool. Because the pack is small for the voltage, plan your cuts in batches and keep a spare charged if you work on a large property.
products.bestFor: Heavier cutting where voltage and a mechanical chain brake matter.
pros: 80V brushless motor delivers strong torque
Mechanical chain brake adds a safety layer
16 inch bar handles larger logs
Maker describes power as 50 cc gas equivalent
cons: 80V packs are heavier and cost more to replace

products.name: Greenworks 40V 12 inch cordless chainsaw kit, 2Ah battery, about 6 lb, dual safety start

specList.label: Battery
specList.value: 2Ah, about 50 cuts of 4x4 per charge per listing

specList.label: Safety
specList.value: Dual safety start, lock plus trigger

products.description:
The Greenworks 40V is a 12 inch saw with a low recoil chain, dual safety start with a lock and trigger and tool free auto tensioning. The listing says a single charge makes about 50 cuts on treated 4x4 lumber, and it weighs about 6 lb with a wrapped grip.

It is a light saw for limbing, pruning and cutting small trees, and it is easy to carry for camping or storm cleanup. The 12 inch bar limits the diameter of what you can cut in one pass, so a 16 inch saw is better for bigger logs. Against the EGO CS1613, it is lighter and cheaper. Against the SEESII 12 inch, it has a smaller battery but a more established brand.

Oil the bar and clean the chain. Replace the chain when it dulls. Its light weight also makes it easier to use at awkward angles, which is where most injuries happen with heavier saws.
products.bestFor: Limbing, pruning and storm cleanup on a small property.
pros: Light at about 6 lb, easy to carry and control
Low recoil chain and dual safety start add safety
Tool free auto tensioning is convenient
Lower price tier than the 16 inch saws
cons: 2Ah battery gives about 50 cuts per the listing

products.name: SEESII 12 inch cordless chainsaw, 1200 W brushless, 2 x 4.0Ah batteries, auto oiling
products.description:
The SEESII 12 inch saw has a 1200 W brushless motor, auto oiling and two 4.0Ah batteries, with tool free tensioning. Two large batteries let you cut longer before a recharge, which is the main advantage over the single battery Greenworks.

The brand is newer and parts support is thinner, so consider the long term. Against the Greenworks 40V 12 inch, it has more batteries and more stated motor power. Against the SEESII 40V 16 inch, it is smaller and lighter. For a homeowner who needs a lot of cutting time, the second battery is valuable.

Check the oil reservoir level before cutting and sharpen the chain regularly. With two packs you can charge one while the other runs, which turns a weekend job into a continuous session.
products.bestFor: Longer yard sessions where two batteries matter.
pros: Two 4.0Ah batteries extend working time
1200 W brushless motor for a 12 inch saw
Auto oiling keeps the bar lubricated
Tool free tensioning
cons: Newer brand with less parts support
Stated motor power is a maker figure

products.name: SEESII 40V 16 inch cordless chainsaw, 2000 W brushless, battery powered

specList.label: Best for
specList.value: Occasional larger cuts on a budget

products.description:
The SEESII 40V 16 inch saw has a native 40V brushless motor that the listing rates at 2000 W, with a 16 inch bar for thicker logs. It aims to give large saw capacity at a lower tier.

The wattage figure is a maker claim, and real performance depends on battery output and chain sharpness. Against the EGO CS1613, it has a lower price tier but also less brand support and a shorter track record. Against the Greenworks 80V, it has lower voltage. If you need a 16 inch bar for occasional cutting, it is a budget route.

Check the battery fit and lubricate the bar. Wear full protective gear. Because support is thin, buy a spare chain and bar oil at the same time so the saw is never stuck waiting for parts.
products.bestFor: Occasional larger cuts when budget is the priority.

products.name: SEESII 6 inch mini cordless chainsaw, 900 W, 2.7 lb, 2 batteries
products.description:
The SEESII mini chainsaw has a 6 inch bar, a 900 W motor and two 21V 2000 mAh batteries, and weighs only 2.7 lb. It is a handheld pruning saw, built for small branches and tidying.

The listing mentions one handed operation, which is something to treat with caution, since a chainsaw is safest with two hands. A mini saw is not a substitute for a full size saw for firewood or felling trees. Against the Greenworks 12 inch, it is far lighter and cuts only small diameters.

Use two hands whenever possible and wear eye and hand protection. Keep the chain oiled and sharpen it. If you only prune ornamental shrubs and fruit trees, a compact saw like this keeps a bigger saw in the shed.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The bar sets the maximum log diameter and the saw's size. A 12 inch bar suits limbing and small trees, a 16 inch bar handles most yard trees and firewood, and a 6 inch mini is for pruning. A bar that is too long for your strength is unsafe, so match length to the job. The usual buyer mistake is buying the longest bar available and then struggling to control it.

Voltage describes power and amp hours describe how long it lasts. The EGO uses 56V with 4.0Ah, the Greenworks 80V uses 2.5Ah and the SEESII has two 4.0Ah packs. Cut counts, like up to 130 cuts on a 4x4, depend on wood and chain sharpness. See our guide on battery voltage and amp hours. Chain sharpening is a skill worth learning, because a sharp chain does more for safety than any extra volts.

Brushless motors are more efficient, cooler and need less maintenance than brushed ones. The EGO, Greenworks 80V and SEESII saws are brushless. A motor's wattage claim is less useful than its torque and the battery that feeds it. Check that spare chains and bars are easy to buy for the model before committing to it.

A mechanical chain brake stops the chain when the front guard is pushed. The Greenworks 80V lists one, and the Greenworks 40V has a dual safety start. Low kickback chains reduce risk. No feature replaces proper gear, a stable stance and a sharp chain. Wear chainsaw chaps even for small jobs, since leg injuries are the most common serious ones.

A chain that is too loose can jump off the bar, and one that is too tight wears quickly. Tool free tensioning, as on the EGO and Greenworks, makes adjustments easier. Auto oiling, as on the SEESII, keeps the bar lubricated, but you must keep the reservoir filled. Choose a saw with a visible oil window so you can see the level without opening a cap.

A saw you cannot control is dangerous. The Greenworks 12 inch weighs about 6 lb and the mini 2.7 lb, while 16 inch saws with batteries are heavier. A heavier saw is steadier but tires you faster. Plan the cut before you start and clear a retreat path, because kickback gives you very little time to react.

specDecoder.meaning: The length of the guide bar in inches, a rough guide to the largest log you can cut. The cutting capacity is a little less than the bar length.
specDecoder.watchFor: A 16 inch bar is not a 16 inch cut capacity in every case, because of the nose and the cut angle.

specDecoder.meaning: A marketing comparison that describes power as similar to a gas saw of a given engine size. It is not a standard measurement.
specDecoder.watchFor: The EGO claims 40 cc and the Greenworks 80V claims 50 cc equivalence.

specDecoder.meaning: A safety device that stops the chain quickly when the front hand guard is pushed forward.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Greenworks 80V lists a mechanical brake, but not all listings detail it.

specDecoder.meaning: The chain pitch is the spacing of drive links and the gauge is the thickness of the drive link. They must match the bar.
specDecoder.watchFor: The EGO lists 3/8 inch pitch and 0.043 inch gauge, so buy matching replacement chains.

specDecoder.meaning: A knob or lever that adjusts chain tension without a wrench.
specDecoder.watchFor: The EGO and Greenworks saws have it, but check tension before each cut.

howWeEvaluated.title: Bar and capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared 6, 12 and 16 inch bars against typical yard jobs. We favoured a match between bar length and the task. We did not cut test any saw. Owner feedback patterns about chain stretch and battery fade shaped our view of ownership cost.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and power
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at voltage platforms from 40V to 80V, battery capacity and stated cut counts. Maker power equivalence claims were treated as marketing. We treated manufacturer cut counts as indicative, since wood species changes everything.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety features
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed chain brakes, dual start and low recoil chains. Features that reduce kickback risk scored higher. Where a listing was silent on a brake we noted the absence.

howWeEvaluated.title: Convenience
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed tool free tensioning, auto oiling and weight. Easier maintenance scored higher. We compared how easy it is to retension the chain without tools.

howWeEvaluated.title: Platform and ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered brand support, chain and bar availability and owner feedback patterns. Established platforms scored higher. Replacement chain and bar availability counted for each brand.

cards.label: 12 inch
cards.text: The Greenworks 40V and SEESII 12 inch are lighter and easier to control. They suit limbing and small logs.

cards.label: 16 inch
cards.text: The EGO, Greenworks 80V and SEESII 16 inch cut larger logs. They are heavier and need more care.

howToChoose.note: Choose 12 inch for yard cleanup and 16 inch if you cut firewood.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A saw that you can carry and control, a chain brake and enough battery for a dozen cuts. Leave leaning or tangled trees to professionals.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Greenworks 40V is light and quick, and the EGO provides a larger battery for longer work.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You cut firewood often or want a platform with other tools. The EGO and Greenworks 80V suit that.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You cut a few limbs a year. The Greenworks 40V or SEESII 12 inch are enough.

maintenance.why: A dull chain forces you to push, which raises kickback risk and drains the battery.
A dry bar overheats and wears quickly. Top up even on auto oiling saws.
A loose chain can derail and a tight chain wears. Adjust when the bar is cool.

maintenance.task: Clean the bar groove and brake area
maintenance.why: Sawdust jams the chain brake and bar. Clear with a stick or brush.
Heat and cold shorten battery life. Store at partial charge.

faq.q: Is a cordless chainsaw powerful enough for firewood?
faq.a: A 16 inch brushless saw on a 56V or 80V platform handles firewood for a typical household, though gas saws still lead for big, continuous jobs. Many owners find that a second chain, kept sharp, saves more time than any upgrade.

faq.q: Is a mini chainsaw a good idea?
faq.a: Only for small branches and pruning. They are not designed for felling or firewood, and one handed use is unsafe. Mix your sharpening with a file guide so every tooth matches.

faq.q: What protective gear do I need?
faq.a: At minimum eye and hearing protection, gloves, sturdy boots and chainsaw chaps. A helmet with a face shield is recommended for tree work. Replace the bar if it shows burrs or heavy wear on the rails.

Keep the chain sharp, avoid cutting with the tip of the bar and hold the saw with both hands. A chain brake and low kickback chain help but do not remove the risk. Let a hot motor cool before storing the saw in a cold shed.

faq.q: How many cuts does one battery make?
faq.a: Listings give figures such as up to 130 cuts on a 4x4 for the EGO, but results vary with wood and chain sharpness. Treat them as a guide. Store the saw with the bar cover on, which also protects your hands.
Only if you have training and the tree is small and clear. Leaning, large or tangled trees are a job for a professional. Never cut above shoulder height, because control drops sharply.
